newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Firmer Irish pound seen set for tight range trade.
newsitem.headline: Firmer Irish pound seen set for tight range trade.

text.p: The Irish pound, hammered on Tuesday by sterling's surge after a British rate rise and news the Bank of England had won its independence, clawed back some intraday losses by mid-morning on Wednesday.
The Irish pound, which had dipped close to 0.91 sterling a day earlier, was holding firm around 0.92 at 0900 GMT and at 2.5939 marks.
Experts predicted a less turbulent time for the punt on Wednesday which slid last week after the central bank indicated it would not intervene to support the punt.

"It's going to be a day of very tight range trading. We would appear for the moment to be caught in a range of 2.5750 to 2.60 marks and I would expect that range to persist today because sterling appears to have topped out at 2.83 and is finding it difficult to stay above 2.8150," Bank of Ireland Group Treasury economist Jim Power said.

Power said market players were taking a breather from the recent turmoil. He said the upside for the Irish pound remained limited, with any attempt to break through 2.60 marks likely to be met by heavy selling pressure.
"I would expect sterling to retrace a little bit and the Irish pound will ease back a little also against the mark."

Dealer said focus was shifting on to the level at which Ireland would joint European Monetary Union against the mark -- around 2.41 marks. They said that put an effective 2.6 mark ceiling on the Irish currency.
Dealers said the Irish pound looked well supported for the time being however and played down talk of possible intervention by the Irish central bank.
They said a move by the Irish pound back below 0.92 sterling and towards 0.91 would not be surprising but was unlikely to happen on Wednesday, barring any spectacular shifts in sterling.
A break below strong support at 0.91 sterling was deemed unlikely for the short term.
